output.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(o.net_revenue) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id), 2) AS avg_revenue_per_customer_2025_eur FROM marts.fct_orders o WHERE o.is_revenue = true AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01';
output.explanation: Revenue counts only completed orders (is_revenue = true). Restricting to order_date in 2025 and dividing total net revenue by the number of distinct customers with at least one completed 2025 order gives the average revenue per customer who bought in 2025. I read "bought something" as having a completed order, since cancelled, returned, or open orders are not treated as purchases elsewhere in the definitions. If you want customers with any order status counted, the denominator would change.
